chunks.label: Men, women, people
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about men, women and people in general.
chunks.interference: otoko and onna sound blunt about a specific person; josei or otoko no hito is the polite choice.

chunks.label: Who someone is to you
chunks.rationale: Lets you say how you know someone: teacher, senior, or just an acquaintance.
chunks.interference: sensei also means a doctor, and senpai is anyone who started before you, not a mentor.

chunks.label: Groups and each other
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about your group, everyone in it, and what you do for each other.
chunks.interference: zen'in (every single member) gets mixed up with minna (everyone, casual).

chunks.label: Checking things
chunks.rationale: Lets you look things up, check, double-check and compare.
chunks.interference: kakunin suru, chekku suru and tashikameru all mean 'check'; shiraberu is finding out something new.

chunks.label: Mistakes and do-overs
chunks.rationale: Lets you say something's wrong, you slipped up, you missed it, or you'll redo it.
chunks.interference: machigau (be wrong) gets mixed up with machigaeru (get X wrong).

chunks.label: How it turned out
chunks.rationale: Lets you say whether something worked, failed, got finished or passed.
chunks.interference: seikou suru sounds big; for everyday things, umaku iku is the natural 'it worked'.

chunks.label: Learning and practice
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about lessons, practice, focus and working out numbers.
chunks.interference: narau needs a teacher, manabu is learning in general, and benkyou suru is studying.

chunks.label: Living your life
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about being alive, how you live and how you spend your time.
chunks.interference: ikiru and kurasu both translate as 'live', but where you live is sumu.

chunks.label: Born and growing up
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about having a baby, where you grew up and how someone has grown.
chunks.interference: umu (give birth) vs umareru (be born), and sodatsu (grow up) vs sodateru (raise).

chunks.label: Work and school habits
chunks.rationale: Lets you say where you work, and that you're running late or skipping.
chunks.interference: chikoku suru is late for a start time; okureru is late in general.

chunks.label: Luck and doing well
chunks.rationale: Lets you say something's good, you're lucky, it's selling, you guessed right, or someone's thriving.
chunks.interference: ateru (guess right) vs ataru (it hits, you win), and ureru (it sells) vs uru (sell it).

chunks.label: Fights and friction
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about fights, rows, bullying and not wanting to do something.
chunks.interference: kenka suru is any fight or argument; momeru is a drawn-out dispute.

chunks.label: Trying and aiming high
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about goals, effort, trying things out and going head to head.
chunks.interference: tamesu tests something and chousen suru takes on something hard; everyday 'try doing' is -te miru.

chunks.label: Getting work done
chunks.rationale: Lets you push a job forward, sort out a problem, wrap things up and take on tasks.
chunks.interference: susumeru (go ahead with) sounds the same as susumeru (recommend).

chunks.label: Lies and getting caught
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about tricking, stealing, covering up and getting caught.

chunks.label: Danger and escape
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about running away, getting dragged into trouble and bad experiences.
chunks.interference: me ni au uses 遭う (run into trouble), not 会う (meet someone).

chunks.label: Polite do and handle
chunks.rationale: Lets you follow shop and office talk about who will do or handle something.
chunks.interference: itasu lowers your own action and nasaru raises the other person's; swapping them is a real blunder.
